## Post

Text from Article: I believe that a ‘pivotal act’ is Yudkowsky’s euphemism for acts of terrorism that he believes anyone making AGI must do under certain circumstances to prevent competition and therefore the end of the world, and that many members of this enterprise will understand some offshoot of this idea and will understand such acts to be necessary in the course of pursuing their goals.
Claim: acts of terrorism that he believes anyone making AGI must do

## Research findings

The claim is misleading. It overstates and mislabels what Yudkowsky means by 'pivotal act'. The article does frame it as the author's own belief ('I believe'), and critics do object to the concept.

1. **Definition.** Yudkowsky's Arbital page defines 'pivotal act' as a guarded term for actions that make a large positive difference a billion years later (https://arbital.com/p/pivotal/). The page stresses that the term should not be stretched. A LessWrong post makes the same point and says the term has a specific meaning (https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/PKBXczqhry7iK3Ruw/pivotal-acts-means-something-specific). The definition does not mention terrorism. It is about changing the long-run outcome of the game.

2. **It involves powerful AI, not human attacks.** AISafety.info says Yudkowsky coined the term and intended an act involving powerful AI. It says a human attack on an AI lab would typically not count under his definition (https://aisafety.info/questions/7580/). That conflicts with the idea that the term is a euphemism for human terrorist acts.

3. **The 'burn all GPUs' example is hypothetical.** In 'AGI Ruin', Yudkowsky says he doesn't actually advocate burning all GPUs. He says the example is a rough overestimate of the power level required. He also says all known pivotal acts are outside the Overton Window (https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/uMQ3cqWDPHhjtiesc/agi-ruin-a-list-of-lethalities). He describes the act as one that stops other actors from destroying the world, and he calls it 'burn all GPUs' only as an illustration (https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/).

4. **'Anyone making AGI must' goes too far.** In 'AGI Ruin' he argues there are no 'pivotal weak acts'. He says mild measures won't stop another lab from destroying the world, while burning all GPUs would (https://www.greaterwrong.com/posts/uMQ3cqWDPHhjtiesc/agi-ruin-a-list-of-lethalities). Critics on the EA Forum read points 5 and 6 as implying that whoever first builds AGI must perform a drastic act. They disagree with that and say the AI safety community should consider other strategies (https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/zzFbZyGP6iz8jLe9n/agi-ruin-a-list-of-lethalities). So the 'must' reading is a contested interpretation, not something Yudkowsky states as a duty of all AGI makers.

5. **Critics do raise legitimacy concerns.** One critic says the concept makes the AI safety community seem 'supervillain-y' (same EA Forum link above). Another says the traditional pivotal act would suppress humanity (https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/JFNjbMXpJYqvgasaK/we-should-think-about-the-pivotal-act-again-here-s-a-better). Holly Elmore calls it a 'coup' (https://lironshapira.substack.com/p/holly-elmore-case-against-eliezer). Yudkowsky himself has said an unaligned-regulation-bypassing pivotal act would have to 'bypass regulators' (https://x.com/ESYudkowsky/status/1438198191296372740). These sources support calling the act unilateral, illegal or coercive. They do not support calling it 'terrorism' by definition, and they do not show it is a euphemism.

I did not re-fetch the 2023 TIME op-ed or Yudkowsky's statements that pivotal acts need not be violent, so I'm not relying on them here.

cascade.findings: Yudkowsky defines a 'pivotal act' as preventing others from building unaligned AGI: "We need to align the performance of some large task, a 'pivotal act' that prevents other people from building an unaligned AGI that destroys the world. While the number of actors with AGI is few or one, they must execute some 'pivotal act', strong enough to flip the gameboard, using an AGI powerful enough to do that" https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/ . His stock example is "burn all GPUs" https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/ , elsewhere described as melting all GPUs globally or subtly changing GPUs so they can't be used for AGI https://forum.nunosempere.com/s/crosspost-ai-regulation-may-be-more-important-than-ai-alignment-for-existential-safety , and as nanomachines that hunt down and burn all GPUs https://manifold.markets/question/is-there-a-pivotal-weak-act . He explicitly acknowledges "all known pivotal acts are currently outside the Overton Window" https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/ . Crucially the act is framed as performed by/using a powerful aligned AGI, not as human builders personally committing violence, and summaries stress "to avoid catastrophe, whoever builds AGI first will have to a) align it... c) do some pivotal act that prevents others from scaling it up" https://lesswrong.com/posts/f4c5BUSfip之类 — i.e. first/few actors, conditional, via AGI. In his 2023 TIME moratorium proposal he advocated state action: participating countries should be willing to take military action such as "destroy[ing] a rogue datacenter by airstrike" to enforce a moratorium https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eliezer_Yudkowsky . That is described as interstate military force / enforcement of international agreements, not non-state terrorism, and other descriptions of pivotal-act proposals include "establish unbreakable international agreements, or develop other mechanisms that make uncontrolled AI development physically impossible" https://github.com/centresecuriteia/aisafety_atlas_multilingual/blob/main/docs/chapters/03/10.md . Calling the whole category "acts of terrorism" that "anyone making AGI must do" therefore conflates AGI-executed disabling of compute and state-enforced moratorium with terrorism, overgeneralizes "first/few under time-limit competition" to "anyone," and treats an openly-discussed extreme-power requirement as a euphemistic cover.

He adds that it is not what you would actually want to do with a powerful AGI. He also writes that he does not actually advocate it. He says it is a rough stand-in for the power level required. He adds that all known pivotal acts are currently outside the Overton Window. https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/ and https://www.alignmentforum.org/posts/uMQ3cqWDPHhjtiesc/agi-ruin-a-list-of-lethalities

Yudkowsky tweeted that a pivotal act 'must bypass regulators'. https://x.com/ESYudkowsky/status/1438198191296372740 Critics such as Holly Elmore call the plan a 'coup'. https://lironshapira.substack.com/p/holly-elmore-case-against-eliezer Others say it would require suppressing humanity. https://forum.effectivealtruism.org/posts/HG6nnjBSradb9oso8/we-should-think-about-the-pivotal-act-again-here-s-a-better So the idea is plausibly read as unilateral and illegal. Calling it 'terrorism' is still the author's characterization. The claim attributes to Yudkowsky a euphemism and a requirement ('must') that he has not stated.

cascade.findings:
Yudkowsky does define a 'pivotal act' as a large task that a first/early aligned AGI-builder must perform to stop others building unaligned AGI that destroys the world: "We need to align the performance of some large task, a 'pivotal act' that prevents other people from building an unaligned AGI that destroys the world. While the number of actors with AGI is few or one, they must execute some 'pivotal act', strong enough to flip the gameboard, using an AGI powerful enough to do that." His illustrative example is "burn all GPUs" https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/ - summarized elsewhere as preventing other actors from building unaligned AGI that kills all humans, e.g. "Releasing nanomachines that hunt down and burn all GPUs is a 'pivotal act'" https://manifold.markets etc., and as "something you can get the aligned superintelligent AI to do to prevent any other labs from building unaligned AI" https://www.lesswrong.com/posts/Lpurs5qXDG8irSDXm/is-ai-alignment-enough . That supports the "must do under certain circumstances to prevent competition/end of world" part.

Calling it "acts of terrorism" is inflammatory/misleading: Yudkowsky frames it as an AI-performed strategic/technological intervention (disabling compute, e.g. melt/burn GPUs, establish agreements, make uncontrolled development physically impossible https://github.com/centresecuriteia/aisafety_atlas_multilingual/blob/main/docs/chapters/03/10.md ), not unlawful anti-civilian violence for political intimidation. His separate human-enforcement proposal was for states to enforce a moratorium, including "be willing to destroy a rogue datacenter by airstrike" https://www.businessinsider.mx etc., reported as "In his notorious TIME op-ed, 'Shut it All Down,' he argued that governments should 'be willing to destroy a rogue datacenter by airstrike.'" https://www.techdirt.com/2025/08/15/the-ai-docs-falsehoods-and-false-balance/ - state military action, not "terrorism," and conditional on violating a global shutdown/moratorium, not an unconditional duty of "anyone making AGI." Yudkowsky explicitly says burn-all-GPUs is "not what I think you'd actually want to do" but "a mild overestimate for the rough power level" https://intelligence.org/2022/06/10/agi-ruin/ , undermining "euphemism for terrorism" claim.
